transcript:
elaine: Hey runtime team — planning a webinar next week and marketing needs an authoritative sanity-run of the benchmark numbers we'll show. Can you rerun a focused smoke suite and confirm methodology? Key asks below.

elaine: What we need: p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, wall-time and cost-per-1k-tokens for the following variants: baseline (fp16), q4_0, q4_1, and a 2-bit quantized build if available. Also include failures/errors and variance across 3 runs.

elaine: Targets: 512 and 2k context lengths, single-request latency profile (no user batching) and a realistic burst load profile (50 concurrent connections, small prompts). We'll call out exact numbers on slides so we need reproducible commands and env.

sam: Ack. Quick clarifying Qs: which model(s) exactly? and do you want server-side KV-cache warm start or cold-cache for the single-request numbers?

elaine: Use the Eng-default model set: rwd/turbo-8k and rwd/llama-13b-quantized (if LLM-13b quant isn't available, use the closest 13B variant). For single-request: cold-cache (first token surface). For burst: warm-cache after a 1-minute priming run.

mira: Also for evaluation: include top-k/top-p sampling settings used, temperature, and prompt templates. Marketing will show one representative prompt per vertical (search summary, chat reply, code comment). I'll attach the prompt file in a follow-up.

sam: Got it. I'll run on the dedicated perf-cluster (pools with A10G). I'll produce a short runbook with exact docker image + git ref + run flags. Expected turnaround ~6 hours from start depending on queue. Any hard SLA? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

elaine: We need this before Tue EOD. If it's tight, a preliminary smoke with fp16 + q4_0 for the 512 context single-request numbers would be ok — but final numbers by Tue.

jordan: Heads up — we're doing node kernel upgrades on the perf cluster tonight at 23:00 UTC. If Sam starts after that, expect ~30m queue; otherwise maybe immediate. Also we'll cap power to 270W for the run; include that in the runbook.

sam: Noted. I'll schedule to start at 00:30 UTC to avoid noisy co-tenants. Plan:

sam: - Repo: github.com/redwood/inference-benchmarks @ refs/heads/webinar-smoke
sam: - Docker: redwood/bench:20260320
sam: - Cmd (example):
```
./run_bench --model rwd/turbo-8k --quant fp16,q4_0,q4_1 --ctx 512,2048 --runs 3 --warmup 60 --burst 50 --prompts=marketing/prompts.json --out=artifacts/webinar_1918765432.json
```

sam: Will also include the exact hw details (GPU model, CUDA/CUDNN, kernel), power cap, and cost calc script.

mira: For stats please include sample sizes, sample variance, and per-prompt breakdown. We'll need p-values if differences are small (marketing wants to claim x% faster — avoid overstating).

elaine: Good call. Please include the raw CSV of token-by-token timing and the Jupyter notebook snippet used to compute the p50/p95 so we can verify numbers.

benchbot: Auto-note: benchmark job queued on perf-cluster-3, est start 00:35 UTC. Job id: bench-20260320-482

sam: Update: first smoke (fp16 + q4_0, ctx 512, single-request) completed. Initial results attached: p50=62ms, p95=142ms (fp16) | p50=78ms, p95=190ms (q4_0). Throughput numbers for burst still running. Uploading artifacts now.

elaine: Thanks — can you post the artifact link here and the run command exact copy so I can put in the appendix?

sam: Artifact: s3://redwood-bench/webinar/1918765432/webinar_fp16_q4_0_512_single.json
sam: Exact run command (copied):
```
./run_bench --model rwd/turbo-8k --quant fp16,q4_0 --ctx 512 --runs 3 --warmup 0 --prompts=marketing/prompts_short.json --out=webinar_fp16_q4_0_512_single.json
```

mira: Quick sanity: do we have tokenization parity between runs? If any run used a different tokeniser build, numbers won't be comparable.

sam: Confirmed same tokenizer build across runs (tokenizer v2.1 from repo lockfile). Also pinned to torch 2.2 and cuda 12.1 in the dockerfile.

jordan: I spot-checked perf node logs — one of the runs had a transient NVLINK error but didn't fail. Sam, include that in the anomalies section and mark which run it was.

sam: Will do. Plan to finish burst/warm runs and the 2k context pass in the next 3 hours. I'll upload final artifacts and a short runbook gist with env and commands.

elaine: Awesome — appreciate the quick turnaround. Once final artifacts are up, marketing will craft a short methodology blurb and will run it by you for technical accuracy before publishing.

sam: Sounds good. I'll ping when everything's done. :white_check_mark:

benchbot: Job bench-20260320-482 completed at 01:48 UTC. Summary uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/webinar/1918765432/summary.txt
